subject: Critical Thinking
title: John Stuart Mill: The Harm Principle and Free Thought
description: A short lesson to help you apply John Stuart Mill: The Harm Principle and Free Thought.

hook.text: John Stuart Mill: a surprising example shows why better reasoning matters.

buildup.text: Mill's harm principle: you can do anything that doesn't harm others.

discovery.text: 'On Liberty': silencing any opinion is wrong — true or false. Suppressing it destroys your ability to defend truth.

twist.text: The difficulty: what counts as 'harm'? Offense? Economic disadvantage? Emotional distress?

climax.text: John Stuart Mill matters because clearer reasoning leads to better judgments.

punchline.text: Your freedom ends where another person's harm begins.

quiz.question: What is Mill's harm principle?
options: Power over individuals is only justified to prevent harm to others
